chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: Playing for Bessie Smith in the Bijou pit
summary: Cheatham played behind Bessie Smith when she lacked a pianist, and explains that TOBA singers were often so poor they could not carry accompanists.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Did you ever hear Bessie Smith?
Did I? I played with Bessie Smith.
I played with Bessie Smith at the Bijou Theater when she came there.
Oh, that's right you mentioned that.

I played with Bessie Smith, sometimes she would have a piano, sometimes she didn't. It depended upon the finances. As I said before, lot of the blues singers when they could afford to carry pianos with them, they did. But sometimes they couldn't because they didn't have the money, they were in arrears with the -- you know -- the --
But when was this, that you played with Bessie Smith?

Well, I played with Bessie at the Bijou Theater. I was in the pit, cause we had to play -- a lot of times we had to play with singers and sometimes we didn't. And most the times, when they'd bring a pianists, they wouldn't use a pit band at all.
But when they didn't have a piano player, why we had to play. Maggie Hargraves was one of the finest of all show piano players and blues piano players alive
at that time. She could play with anyone. Well I played with Bessie -- the year I don't remember. It couldn't of been in '25. I could've been somewhere around '25. Late '25.
Well, if it was '25, then surely Bessie could've afforded a pianist at that time, right, she was very big at that time.

Well, she was big, yes, but you'd be surprised at the times when they were -- as I said before this was all money. They came through there some of them, well the TOBA was the only way of making a living. And it was rough, because they wasn't getting paid, half the time. Lot of times they couldn't afford a piano player.
And there was some piano players that just went along with them, worked with Bessie or the rest of the piano players just for expenses because they couldn't do any better themselves.
They would get their hotel, food and afew dollars. There were times when those other blues singers were in destitute circumstances. Including Bessie Smith.
